Color Schemes

Source: vignettes/articles/color-schemes.Rmd
color-schemes.Rmd

Choose a color scheme according to what color means in the plot. Categories need distinct colors that remain easy to tell apart. Numeric values need an ordered progression whose intermediate colors also have meaning.

The examples use the same iris PCA as the Getting Started article:

library(vizier)

pca_iris <- stats::prcomp(iris[, -5], retx = TRUE, rank. = 2)

Choose categorical or continuous behavior

Vizier derives the mapping behavior from the value supplied as x:

  • A factor or character vector is categorical. Each observed value receives one color from the palette.
  • A numeric vector is continuous. Values are mapped across a color ramp, so an ordered palette is usually the right choice.
  • colors supplies literal per-observation colors and bypasses palette mapping.

For categories, the default is R’s stable "Polychrome 36" palette when it is available, with an HCL Dynamic fallback. Numeric values default to a sequential HCL Viridis palette.

Specify a palette

The color_scheme argument accepts:

  • A function that takes an integer n and returns n colors, such as grDevices::rainbow.
  • An unnamed vector of at least two colors, used as a positional palette.
  • A fully named vector, used as a category-to-color mapping.
  • A paletteer name in "package::palette" form, optionally followed by a type override such as ::c or ::continuous.
  • The name of a built-in R palette, such as "Okabe-Ito" on R 4.0 or later.

Palette functions

A palette function generates exactly the number of colors Vizier requests:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = grDevices::topo.colors
)
Iris species colored with the first three colors generated by topo.colors

Custom vectors and named mappings

An unnamed vector assigns colors by category position. Naming the same vector locks each color to a category, which keeps the mapping stable after reordering or subsetting:

custom_colors <- c("black", "red", "gray")
embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, color_scheme = custom_colors)

species_colors <- c(
  setosa = "black",
  versicolor = "red",
  virginica = "gray"
)
embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, color_scheme = species_colors)
Setosa in black, versicolor in red, and virginica in gray

The two calls produce the same full-data plot here. For a named mapping, extra names are ignored and every observed category must have a color.

If an unnamed vector has fewer colors than Vizier needs, Vizier interpolates between its colors. That is appropriate only when the vector represents a meaningful progression. Set verbose = TRUE to report when interpolation is required.

Built-in R palette names

On R 4.0 or later, pass any name returned by grDevices::palette.pals():

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "Okabe-Ito"
)
Iris species colored with the first three Okabe-Ito colors

Paletteer names

paletteer provides a common name for palettes from many R packages. Use "package::palette", for example:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Dark2"
)
Iris species colored with the RColorBrewer Dark2 palette

Vizier looks up whether paletteer classifies the selected palette as continuous, fixed-width discrete, or dynamic and calls the corresponding paletteer generator. It does not collapse those types into one behavior.

Reverse generated colors

Set rev = TRUE to reverse a generated palette before Vizier maps it to categories or numeric values:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = turbo
)
Iris species colored with Vizier’s turbo palette
embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = turbo,
  rev = TRUE
)
The same iris species with the turbo palette order reversed

Reversal also applies to named category mappings, while preserving their names. It does not reorder literal per-row colors supplied through colors.

Sample a discrete palette across its full extent

By default, requesting three colors from a fixed-width discrete palette takes its first three colors. Appending ::c or ::continuous tells paletteer to treat that palette as continuous and sample across its full extent instead. The explicit ::d and ::discrete suffixes select the default discrete behavior.

This choice is useful only when the order and intermediate colors have a meaningful progression.

A qualitative palette: Dark2

The full RColorBrewer::Dark2 palette contains unrelated qualitative colors:

paletteer::paletteer_d("RColorBrewer::Dark2")
Eight distinct qualitative colors in the RColorBrewer Dark2 palette

The default discrete behavior uses the first three colors:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Dark2",
  cex = 2,
  title = "RColorBrewer Dark2"
)
Iris species colored with the first three Dark2 colors

Forcing continuous sampling uses the two ends of the palette and synthesizes a middle color between them:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Dark2::c",
  cex = 2,
  title = "RColorBrewer Dark2 (continuous)"
)
Dark2 sampled as a continuous scale, with a brown middle cluster close to the gray cluster

The synthesized brown is not one of Dark2’s original colors and is less distinct from the gray endpoint. Continuous sampling therefore weakens this qualitative palette rather than improving it.

An ordered palette: jcolors rainbow

The jcolors::rainbow palette has a visible red-to-purple order:

paletteer::paletteer_d("jcolors::rainbow")
Nine ordered colors progressing from red through green and blue to purple

Default discrete behavior again uses the first three colors, so all three iris species stay near the red-to-green end:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "jcolors::rainbow",
  cex = 2,
  title = "jcolors rainbow"
)
Iris species colored with the first three jcolors rainbow colors

The continuous override spreads three samples across the entire ordered palette:

embed_plot(
  pca_iris$x,
  iris$Species,
  color_scheme = "jcolors::rainbow::c",
  cex = 2,
  title = "jcolors rainbow (continuous)"
)
Iris species colored from the red, middle blue, and purple regions of the full rainbow palette

Here, sampling the full extent preserves the palette’s intended order and makes better use of its range. For unordered qualitative palettes, keep the default discrete behavior.

Reproduce the article figures

The tracked vignettes/articles/reproduce-figures.R script generates every figure in this article using the public Vizier and paletteer interfaces. It draws the swatches with base graphics, so no swatch package is required:

Rscript --vanilla vignettes/articles/reproduce-figures.R \
  --output-dir /tmp/vizier-article-figures
